#### Biomass {.tabset .tabset-dropdown}

In the experiment we studied two-patch meta-ecosystems in which we manipulated the size of their patches and their connection (unconnected vs connected). Now, we want to know whether meta-ecosystem size influenced the effects of connection on this response variable. Therefore, we start by looking at how this response variable changed across time for all meta-ecosystems through its mean ± 95 confidence interval:

```{r fig.height = figures_height_rmd_output}
ggarrange(plot.metaecos.legend(ds_metaecosystems %>% filter(size_effects == "fixed"),
                              response_variable),
          plot.metaecos.points(ds_metaecosystems %>% filter(size_effects == "fixed"),
                               response_variable)  +
            rremove("xlab") +
            theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
                  axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
                  legend.position = "none") +
            font("legend.text", size = size_legend) +
            font("ylab", size = size_y_axis) + 
            ggtitle(fixed_label),
          plot.metaecos.points(ds_metaecosystems %>% filter(size_effects == "relative"),
                               response_variable)  +
            font("xlab", size = size_y_axis) +
            font("ylab", size = size_y_axis) +
            scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(ds_metaecosystems$day)) +
            theme(legend.position = "none") +
            ggtitle(relative_label),
          heights = c(0.25, 0.6, 0.6),
          nrow = 3,
          align = "v")
```

<details>

<summary>Click here to view the same data represented through single comparisons </summary>

```{r fig.height = figures_height_rmd_output}
sizes = levels(ds_metaecosystems$size)
p = NULL

"% of disturbance and resource flows are FIXED"
for(i in 1:length(sizes)){
  
  p[[i]] = plot.metaecos.points(ds_metaecosystems %>% 
                                  filter(size_effects == "fixed",
                                         size == sizes[i]),
                                response_variable) + 
    theme(legend.position = "none")
    
}
gridExtra::grid.arrange(p[[1]], 
                        p[[2]], 
                        p[[3]], 
                        p[[4]], 
                        nrow = 2, 
                        ncol = 2)

"% of disturbance and resource flows are RELATIVE to size"
for(i in 1:length(sizes)){
  
  p[[i]] = plot.metaecos.points(ds_metaecosystems %>% 
                         filter(size_effects == "relative",
                                size == sizes[i]),
                       response_variable) + 
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}
gridExtra::grid.arrange(p[[1]], 
                        p[[2]], 
                        p[[3]], 
                        p[[4]], 
                        nrow = 2, 
                        ncol = 2)
```
